title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on How to Handle the Voluntary Repayment of Illicit Money by the Defendant's Relatives on Behalf of the Defendant

articles.content_en:
1. Where the defendant is an adult and all of his or her illegal gains have been squandered by himself or herself and cannot be recovered, the defendant shall be ordered to make restitution, and the family members of the defendant shall have no obligation to make restitution on his or her behalf.
Where the defendant has a personal share in the family common property, the defendant may only be ordered to make restitution within the scope of his or her personal share.

2. Where part of the defendant's illegal gains has been used for the daily life of the family, both the defendant and the family members shall have the obligation to make restitution for that part of the illegal gains.

3. Where the defendant has no actual ability to make restitution for the illegal gains that he or she has been ordered to make restitution for, but the defendant's relatives, at the request of the defendant or on their own initiative and with the defendant's consent, voluntarily make restitution for part or all of the illegal gains on behalf of the defendant, the court may also, taking into account the specific circumstances, accept the funds voluntarily paid by the relatives on behalf of the defendant, and shall deem such funds as voluntarily made by the defendant.

4. Where restitution has been made in any of the above three circumstances, it may be deemed that the defendant has made relatively good restitution of the illegal gains, and a lenient penalty may be imposed as deemed appropriate.

5. Where the defendant's crime is punishable by death and the death penalty must be enforced, if the case falls under the first or second circumstance above, the court may accept the funds paid as restitution; if the case falls under the third circumstance above, the court shall not accept the funds voluntarily paid by the relatives on behalf of the defendant.
August 26, 1987
